sentences.text:
1. In the written instructions supplied by Mr. Krutik Parikh, learned Assistant Government Pleader,
appearing for the State respondents, it is brought on record that the award passed in favour of the petitioner herein was a consent award.

The said fact is noted in the award at page '30' of the paper Dineshbhai Keshubhai Vaghasiya vs National High Speed Rail Corporation ... on 9 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/169179402/
1 book.

entities.text: Dineshbhai Keshubhai Vaghasiya vs National High Speed Rail Corporation
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: A copy of the consent agreement dated 16.05.2020 signed by the petitioner has been placed before us, which is taken on record.
2. We may note that there is no disclosure in the writ petition about the award being consent award.

By concealment of NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/9246/2024 ORDER DATED: 09/07/2024 undefined correct facts, the petitioner seeks to challenge the order passed by the Collector of rejection of application under Section 64 of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 for making a reference.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: From a perusal of the terms and conditions of the consent agreement, it is evident that the petitioner has agreed that he would not take recourse to Section 64 of the Act, 2013.
3. The present petition is, therefore, liable to be dismissed and is, thus, dismissed.

(SUNITA AGARWAL, CJ ) (PRANAV TRIVEDI,J) BIJOY B. PILLAI Dineshbhai Keshubhai Vaghasiya vs National High Speed Rail Corporation ... on 9 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/169179402/

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
By concealment of NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/9246/2024 ORDER DATED: 09/07/2024 undefined correct facts, the petitioner seeks to challenge the order passed by the Collector of rejection of application under Section 64 of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 for making a reference.
From a perusal of the terms and conditions of the consent agreement, it is evident that the petitioner has agreed that he would not take recourse to Section 64 of the Act, 2013.
